**Short answer: I can't tell yet — and I won't guess.** Here's what your records actually show:

- **Reading:** no attempts at all.

- **Error evidence:** still zero logged, so there's no track record of any kind to analyse.

Even a *submitted* attempt would only hold a score and date — it wouldn't show how your answers changed from first pick to final pick. So this specific habit needs its own capture.

Plainly: I also have **no verified OET source** on whether last-second changes help or hurt, so I'm not handing you a "never change" rule. What I can give you is a way to measure it on your own performance:

**How we'd measure it**
1. In practice, tally every question where you change an answer: **original → final**, then after scoring mark which was correct. Two counts: **saves** (wrong→right) and **costs** (right→wrong).
2. Don't read anything into it until you have ~10+ changed answers across a few sessions — below that it's noise.
3. Then read the net: saves minus costs. Clearly negative = it's hurting you; positive = helping; near zero = not a real factor, so adopt one consistent policy and stop burning time deliberating.

**Where:** [Reading drills](https://app.oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/reading/drills) and [Listening practice](https://app.oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/listening). Start by finishing one of those unfinished Listening attempts end-to-end, so scored data begins to exist.

Tonight, protecting what you've got beats adding anything new.

- At most one short, light pass over material you've already done — then stop. Nothing new.
- Sort logistics: route, alarm, breakfast, what you're taking. For what's allowed at the venue, follow the official instructions you were sent — I don't have verified OET exam-day rules on my side.
- Sleep on time. That's the highest-value item tonight.

**Tomorrow before the test**
- Use the approach you already have — one method, no switching mid-paper.
- The last-second answer-changing habit you flagged earlier: don't deliberate over it. Pick one default and keep moving.
- Keep pacing steady; don't rush the reading to "save time."

**Don't spend time on**
- New strategies or tricks (Reading especially) · new vocabulary lists · a full mock test · rebuilding your whole method.
